CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE — level: full

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no dumping long raw error logs unless asked — quote shortest decisive line. Standard well-known tech acronyms OK (DB/API/HTTP); never invent new abbreviations (cfg/impl/req/res/fn) — tokenizer split them same as full word: zero token saved, reader still decode. Full word cheaper AND clearer. No causal arrows (→) either — own token, save nothing. Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Preserve user's dominant language. User write Portuguese → reply Portuguese caveman. User write Spanish → reply Spanish caveman. Compress the style, not the language. No forced English openings or status phrases. ALWAYS keep technical terms, code, API names, CLI commands, commit-type keywords (feat/fix/...), and exact error strings verbatim — unless user explicitly ask for translation.

No self-reference. Never name or announce the style. No "caveman mode on", "me caveman think", no third-person caveman tags. Output caveman-only — never normal answer plus "Caveman:" recap. Exception: user explicitly ask what the mode is.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman. No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no long raw error-log dumps unless asked. Standard acronyms OK; no invented abbreviations |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman when:
- Security warnings
- Irreversible action confirmations
- Multi-step sequences where fragment order or omitted conjunctions risk misread
- Compression itself creates technical ambiguity (e.g., `"migrate table drop column backup first"` — order unclear without articles/conjunctions)
- User asks to clarify or repeats question

Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example — destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

Output format `path:line: <emoji> <severity>: <problem>. <fix>.` Use for "review this PR", "review my diff", "audit this file". Skips formatting nits unless they change meaning. (Tools: Read, Grep, Bash)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## context7
Use this server to fetch current documentation whenever the user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool, or cloud service — even well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. This includes API syntax, configuration, version migration, library-specific debugging, setup instructions, and CLI tool usage. Use even when you think you know the answer — your training data may not reflect recent changes. Prefer this over web search for library docs.

Do not use for: refactoring, writing scripts from scratch, debugging business logic, code review, or general programming concepts.

## plugin:github:github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

## railway
Railway MCP server. Manage your Railway projects, services, deployments, and more.

# macapp/CLAUDE.md

The Workroom macOS app: a SwiftUI (macOS 15+) front-end that bundles the `workroom`
Go binary and drives it over the CLI's `--json` contract. See README.md for full
architecture, signing, and notarization detail — this file is the quick reference.

## Dev tasks (Makefile)

Every dev task runs through the **repo-root `Makefile`**, namespaced `app-*` (run from the repo
root, not `macapp/`):

```bash
make app-run        # canonical local loop: xcodegen → xcodebuild (Debug) → relaunch
make app-build      # xcodegen → xcodebuild (Debug)
make app-test       # xcodebuild test (WorkroomAppTests) — parallel; APP_TEST_FLAGS= to serialize
make app-generate   # force-regenerate the (gitignored) .xcodeproj from project.yml
make app-vcs        # build the Rust VCS core → WrVcs SwiftPM package (auto-run before app builds)
make app-format     # swift-format, rewrite sources in place
make app-lint       # swift-format --strict (non-zero on any violation — the hard gate)
make app-release    # Release build → notarize → staple → DMG installer (Scripts/release.sh)
make app-icon       # regenerate AppIcon PNGs (Scripts/make-icon.swift)
make app-clean      # remove DerivedData + .xcodeproj
```

Builds reuse `macapp/DerivedData/` so the Swift packages (incl. the GhosttyKit xcframework)
aren't re-resolved/re-downloaded every build. (`cli-*` targets cover the Go CLI — see the root
CLAUDE.md.)

## VCS core (Rust jj + SwiftGitX git)

Workroom reads VCS data through **two backends behind one Swift layer** (the app is growing into a
VCS-first IDE — issue #59 is the first brick):

- **jj → Rust `jj-lib` via UniFFI.** The `vcs/` Rust workspace (jj-only) builds a static xcframework
  + generated Swift into the local SwiftPM package `vcs/swift/WrVcs` — the app does `import WrVcs`.
- **git → SwiftGitX (libgit2), pure Swift.** git has a mature native Swift path; jj has none — so
  only jj needs the Rust/UniFFI bridge. (An all-Rust core with gix was tried and dropped: gix bought
  no real unification and libgit2 is the more complete git engine.)

**Three reads reach past SwiftGitX**, all linking the `libgit2` C API **directly** (its own SPM package
in `project.yml`, URL + version identical to SwiftGitX's own dependency so SwiftPM sees one package
identity). `Core/LibGit2.swift` owns the single `git_libgit2_init` and hands out raw `git_repository`
handles (SwiftGitX inits inside `Repository.open`, which a direct C caller can't rely on); these four
files are the only ones in the app touching raw libgit2:

- **Push state — `Core/GitGraph.swift`.** SwiftGitX cannot express a commit *range*: its
  `CommitSequence` only calls `git_revwalk_push`, never `git_revwalk_hide`, it exposes no
  merge-base/graph helper, and its repository pointer is `internal` — so "which commits aren't on
  `origin` yet" (`HEAD --not refs/remotes/origin/*`) needs the C API. The jj side answers the same
  question natively with one `ancestors(<tracked @origin tips>)` revset. Push state is
  **origin-scoped** and any unreadable ref degrades the WHOLE page to "unknown" (no badge) rather than
  a partial answer.
- **Commit diffs — `Core/GitCommitDiff.swift`.** Rename detection is `git_diff_find_similar` run over a
  live `git_diff`, and a SwiftGitX `Diff` materializes its deltas/patches in an `internal` init and
  frees the `git_diff` before returning, so there's nothing left to detect on. Without it a committed
  rename read as delete + add while `git show` showed one rename row (git defaults to
  `diff.renames=true`), and a root commit's diff came back empty (SwiftGitX diffs it against itself).
  Detection options are NULL, which is what makes libgit2 read the repo's own `diff.renames` /
  `diff.renamelimit` — naming a flag explicitly suppresses that config read, so a repo set to
  `diff.renames=false` or `=copies` would silently disagree with its own CLI. Typechanges are included
  (`GIT_DIFF_INCLUDE_TYPECHANGE`); without it libgit2 splits a file↔symlink change into delete + add
  on the SAME path, giving the file list two rows with one `id`. `GitProvider.changeset`/`.fileDiff`
  both read through it, so the History file list and the patch text can't disagree.
- **Working-tree ± line counts — `Core/GitDiffStats.swift`**, via `git_diff_get_stats`. SwiftGitX
  surfaces no diffstat, and its `Diff` is **eager**: `Diff.init` builds a `Patch` per delta and
  materializes every hunk line into a Swift `String` before the caller sees it. Summing those for the
  badge cost one `String` per changed line of the whole worktree on **every** status refresh, so the
  counts moved to libgit2, which counts in C and allocates nothing Swift-side. The diff itself is
  irreducible — that's what `git diff --shortstat` costs too. With `changeset` now counting through
  `GitCommitDiff`, **no** `+N −M` in the app is summed off SwiftGitX hunk lines any more, which also
  ends a real bug: that sum counted the EOFNL markers (`\ No newline at end of file`) as lines, so
  changing only a file's trailing newline reported two deletions where git reports `1 insertion(+),
  1 deletion(-)`. libgit2 skips them, as `git diff --shortstat`/`--numstat` do. It runs
  `git_diff_find_similar` too, for the same reason `GitCommitDiff` does: the file list beside these
  counts already pairs renames (libgit2 status' `.renamesIndex`/`.renamesWorkingTree`), so without it
  a staged rename rendered as one "renamed" row badged `+N −N` while `git diff HEAD --shortstat`
  reported `0 insertions(+), 0 deletions(-)`.

**Read surface & routing.** `Core/VCSProviding.swift` is the one Swift protocol; `VCS.provider(for:)`
routes by repo kind. `RustJJProvider` maps `WrVcs.*` → app-native models, `GitProvider` wraps
SwiftGitX. `WorkroomStatusResolver` and `BranchResolver` read through this layer — **the jj CLI
parsers are gone** (log/changeset/currentRef/workingStatus are all native jj-lib).

**The one mutating read: `RustJJProvider.workingStatus`.** jj's working copy is itself a commit, so
on-disk edits don't exist to jj-lib until snapshotted — a working-copy status read therefore *must*
snapshot `@` first: it takes the working-copy lock and rewrites `@` (modeled on jayjay's
`refresh_working_copy`). Everything else (log/changeset/currentRef) is a read-only `load_at_head`
with no lock. Because it mutates, **only test snapshot changes on throwaway repos** (corruption
risk). Line counts come from the SAME native read — `changed_files` materializes each changed file's
two sides and counts them, so `resolveJJ` fires no `jj diff --stat` process (it used to; see
`40456bae`). Oversized and binary files report no count rather than being read whole. Cargo coverage:
`vcs/crates/wr-vcs-core/tests/working_status.rs` + `line_stats.rs`; Swift coverage:
`WorkroomStatusIntegrationTests.testJJ*`.

`make app-vcs` (→ `vcs/scripts/build-apple.sh`) builds the Rust artifacts and **runs automatically
before `app-build`/`app-test`/`app-generate`** (a Makefile prerequisite). Requirements:

- **`protoc`** on PATH (`brew install protobuf`) — a build-time dep of jj-lib.
- arm64 by default; **`make app-release` builds universal** (`VCS_APPLE_FLAGS=--universal`), which
  needs **rustup `stable` ≥ 1.93** + `rustup target add x86_64-apple-darwin aarch64-apple-darwin`
  (Homebrew's rust can't cross-compile; the script preflights this and errors clearly).
- **Unchanged inputs are a no-op.** The script hashes the Rust sources, manifests/lockfile, itself,
  `rustc --version` and the arch flavour into `vcs/swift/WrVcs/Frameworks/.build-stamp`, and exits
  early when that matches and the outputs exist. `WR_VCS_FORCE=1 make app-vcs` rebuilds regardless.
  CI leans on this: it caches the *outputs* keyed on the same inputs, so a commit that doesn't touch
  `vcs/` skips the ~4-minute crate-graph build (and `make app-test`'s own `app-vcs` prerequisite
  stays free).
- **Xcode-driven builds are gated, not auto-fixed.** ⌘R/⌘U (and a raw `xcodebuild`) skip the
  Makefile, so they'd otherwise link the last-built core. A `Rust VCS core up to date` pre-build
  phase runs `build-apple.sh --check` and **fails the build** with `run 'make app-vcs'` when the
  stamp doesn't match `vcs/`. It can't rebuild for you: SPM extracts the binaryTarget's xcframework
  before target build phases run, so a fresh `.a` wouldn't reach that build's link. Silently linking
  a stale core cost a debugging session once — conflicted files read as `.modified` because the
  linked core predated a merged per-file-conflict fix.

The xcframework + generated Swift are **gitignored and regenerated**; only `Package.swift` + a
`shim.c` are tracked. Packaging note: the xcframework is **library-only** (no headers) and the FFI
Clang module (`wr_vcs_uniffiFFI`) is a separate SPM C target — a headers-bearing static xcframework
copies its `module.modulemap` into the shared `Debug/include/` and collides with GhosttyKit's
("Multiple commands produce include/module.modulemap").

## Formatting & linting

Swift is formatted/linted with **swift-format** (bundled with the Xcode toolchain — run via
`xcrun swift-format`, no install). Config `macapp/.swift-format` (2-space, 100 cols) covers
`WorkroomApp/` + `WorkroomAppTests/` only (not the `Scripts/*.swift` tools). Use `make app-format`
/ `make app-lint`. Every Xcode/`xcodebuild` build also runs a `swift-format lint` pre-build phase
that surfaces violations as **warnings** (non-fatal — `make app-lint` is the hard gate). Run
`make app-format` before committing.

## Gotchas

- **The Swift module is `Workroom`** (the target is `WorkroomApp`; `PRODUCT_MODULE_NAME` is pinned
  to `Workroom` in `project.yml`). Tests use `@testable import Workroom`. The pin matters because
  `PRODUCT_NAME` is **per-config**: `Workroom` for Release, `Workroom Dev` for Debug (see below) —
  without the pin the Debug module would become `Workroom_Dev` and break the import. A test
  target's `TEST_HOST` must point at the Debug product (`Workroom Dev.app/Contents/MacOS/Workroom
  Dev`); XcodeGen's auto-derived (target-name-based) host is wrong and fails with "Could not find
  test host".
- **Debug builds run side by side with the release build.** The Debug config has a distinct
  identity — bundle id `com.developwithstyle.workroom.dev`, product/display name `Workroom Dev`,
  and the amber `AppIcon-Dev` icon set — so a local build doesn't fight the installed release
  `Workroom` for activation, the key window, preferences (separate UserDefaults domain via the
  bundle id), or the system-wide ⌘§ hotkey. The Debug build deliberately **doesn't register ⌘§**
  and **doesn't run Sparkle scheduled checks** (`#if DEBUG` in `WorkroomApp.swift` / `Updater.swift`)
  so it can't grab the global hotkey or try to "update" itself to the release DMG. Both builds
  still share the CLI config at `~/.config/workroom/config.json` (the bundled CLI has no
  config-path override), so they show the same projects/workrooms. `make app-run` only kills the
  `Workroom Dev` instance, never your release build. The two app icons (`make app-icon` renders
  both) are identical except for the tile gradient.
- **Adding/removing/renaming a `.swift` file needs an `xcodegen generate`.** XcodeGen
  expands the source glob into explicit file refs in the (gitignored) `.xcodeproj`, so
  the change is invisible (or, for a deleted/renamed file, a hard "Build input file
  cannot be found" error) until the project is regenerated. The `make app-*` build
  targets now run `xcodegen generate` every time, so this is handled automatically —
  it only bites when building from Xcode directly (regenerate, or run `make app-generate`).
- **SourceKit "Cannot find type X in scope" is usually noise.** The single-file indexer
  doesn't see sibling files; a clean `xcodebuild` is authoritative.
- **The terminal is libghostty** (`libghostty-spm`'s `GhosttyKit` xcframework, pinned
  `exactVersion: 1.2.3` in project.yml). The embedding C API is not yet stable, so pin EXACT —
  don't float it. The terminal surface (`Core/GhosttySurfaceView.swift`) + runtime
  (`GhosttyApp`/`GhosttyRuntimeAdapter`) are ours; the bundled `Resources/ghostty` (terminfo +
  shell-integration) must ship for the engine to start. Pre-GA, the plan is to move to a
  self-built xcframework from a pinned Ghostty fork.
- **The child environment has two layers, and only one of them is reliable** (`Core/ShellEnvironment.swift`).
  A Finder-launched `.app` gets a minimal PATH, so: the **floor** (`floorPath()`) reads `/etc/paths`
  + `/etc/paths.d/*` — `path_helper`'s own inputs — with no shell at all, and that alone resolves
  Postgres.app's `psql`; the **probe** (`refresh()`) then runs one `$SHELL -ilc` for what only an
  interactive login shell knows (`.zshrc` PATH entries, mise shims). The probe is best-effort by
  design: its failures degrade to the floor, so a `.zshrc` that ends `exec tmux` costs enrichment
  and never the bug. Three traps worth knowing: **`path_helper` APPENDS** the PATH it's handed, so
  the probe must be spawned with a *cleared* `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin` or Homebrew ends
  up at the tail; the payload is a **raw `env -0` stream between UUID markers** because command
  substitution strips NULs and the user's `base64` may be GNU's (wraps at 76 cols); and the deadline
  is a `DispatchWorkItem` **inside** the blocking closure, because `withTimeout` cannot cancel a
  `runBlocking` call and would leak a shell per invocation. `setenv("PATH", …)` happens exactly once,
  in `WorkroomApp.init` — a later write would race the status sweep's `ProcessInfo.environment`
  reads. Everything else reads `ShellEnvironment.path()` (PATH only, for the automatic sweep) or
  `.environment()` (the full environment, for setup/teardown scripts).
- **Menu enable/disable must flow through `focusedSceneValue` + `@FocusedValue`**
  (see `WorkroomApp.swift`); a `Commands` body does not re-evaluate when the shared
  `AppStore` mutates. ⌘1–9 are handled by an `NSEvent` local monitor in `AppDelegate`,
  not menu items, so they fire before the terminal swallows the keys.

## Layout

**VCS info that only the GUI needs** (e.g. the sidebar root row's current branch/bookmark)
is resolved app-side in `Core/BranchResolver.swift` (per project, async, with a per-call
timeout) — deliberately NOT added to the `workroom --json` contract, which the human CLI
never shows.

`WorkroomApp/Core/` — store, CLI wrapper, terminal sessions, models, theme.
`WorkroomApp/Views/` — `NavigationSplitView` tree sidebar + terminal detail.
`Scripts/` — `run.sh` (local), `build-helper.sh` (embeds+signs the Go binary), `release.sh`
(build → notarize → staple → DMG → EdDSA-sign for Sparkle), `appcast.sh` (publishes the Sparkle
appcast to the fixed `appcast` release), `appcast-notes.sh` (re-renders a published item's
`<description>` from the current release body — see "Auto-update" below), `make-icon.swift`
(regenerates the `AppIcon` PNGs in `Assets.xcassets` — run `swift Scripts/make-icon.swift`).

## Auto-update (Sparkle)

`Core/Updater.swift` wraps Sparkle's `SPUStandardUpdaterController` (the "Check for Updates…"
menu item + the Settings toggle bind to it). The `SU*` keys in `project.yml` (`SUFeedURL`,
`SUPublicEDKey`, `SUEnableAutomaticChecks`) configure it. **Versioning is tag-driven** —
`CFBundleShortVersionString`/`CFBundleVersion` resolve from `$(MARKETING_VERSION)`/
`$(CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION)`, which `release.sh` injects from the git tag (build number =
commit count, so it only ever increases — Sparkle compares it). The appcast feed is an asset
on the fixed `appcast` GitHub release. See `README.md` ("Auto-update") for the one-time keypair
setup and the `SPARKLE_PRIVATE_KEY` secret.

**Release channels (issue #91) — two build identities.** The **main** app (`Release` config)
switches `stable`⟷`pre` at runtime via the *Settings ▸ General ▸ Release channel* picker
(`ReleaseChannel.pickerCases` = stable/pre only). **Workroom Nightly** is a separate side-by-side
product — the `Nightly` build config in `project.yml` (bundle id `…workroom.nightly`, name, violet
`AppIcon-Nightly`, `WORKROOM_RELEASE_CHANNEL=nightly` → the `WorkroomReleaseChannel` Info.plist
marker read by `ReleaseChannel.current`/`isNightlyBuild`), extending the Debug/"Workroom Dev"
per-config identity pattern to a third identity.

`Updater.allowedChannels(for:)` returns `{nightly}` on the nightly build and the picked stable/pre
floor otherwise; one appcast feed carries all channels (`Scripts/appcast.sh` tags items via the
shared `Scripts/channel-helper.sh`; stable stays untagged = Sparkle default), and Sparkle's
bundle-id check stops either identity installing the other's DMG. Nightly is a single **rolling**
item; appcast idempotency keys on `(channel, build)`. `build-helper.sh` bakes both
`-X main.version=$(MARKETING_VERSION)` and `-X main.channel=$(WORKROOM_RELEASE_CHANNEL)` into the
bundled CLI, and `CommandLineInstaller` symlinks it as `workroom` (main) or `workroom-nightly`
(nightly build) so both coexist in PATH. `Updater.migrateReleaseChannelIfNeeded` opts an upgrading
beta user into `pre` and coerces a legacy `.nightly` selection to `.stable` (main build only).

**Release-notes in the update dialog.** Sparkle's dialog renders the appcast item's
`<description>`. `appcast.sh` (run during the release) embeds the GitHub release body as that
description — but at release time the body is still goreleaser's raw commit list, since the
curated notes are written afterwards. So a second path keeps them in sync: the
`.github/workflows/appcast-notes.yml` workflow fires on every `release: edited` event and runs
`Scripts/appcast-notes.sh`, which re-renders the matching item's `<description>` from the
release's *current* body. Curating a release's notes therefore auto-refreshes what the update
dialog shows; no rebuild needed. To fix an already-published feed by hand, run it directly:
`TAG=vX.Y.Z REPO=owner/repo GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) macapp/Scripts/appcast-notes.sh`.

3	@testable import Workroom

5	/// `CLIVCSWriter` against REAL git and jj repos through the REAL `StatusCommandRunner`.
6	///
7	/// **No network.** Every "remote" is a bare repo on disk reached over `file://`, so fetch, push and
8	/// pull are genuine end-to-end operations with no credentials, no rate limits and no flakiness. Every
9	/// repo is a throwaway under `NSTemporaryDirectory()`, removed in `tearDown` — these never touch a
10	/// developer's own repositories.
11	///
12	/// Two tests here exist specifically to pin bugs that shipped in the design and were caught in review:
13	/// - `testCountsAreIdenticalUnderEveryPushDefault` — the original design read ahead/behind from
14	///   `%(push:track)`, which is EMPTY for a branch with no upstream under git's default
15	///   `push.default=simple`, i.e. for every `git worktree add -b` workroom.
16	/// - `testFetchAtTheRootMovesAWorkroomsLastFetchLabel` — `FETCH_HEAD` is per-worktree, so fetching at
17	///   the project root never writes the workroom's copy; reading the wrong one meant "never fetched"
18	///   forever.
19	final class VCSRemoteIntegrationTests: XCTestCase {
20	  private var dirs: [String] = []
21	
22	  override func tearDown() {
23	    for d in dirs { try? FileManager.default.removeItem(atPath: d) }
24	    dirs = []
25	    super.tearDown()
26	  }
27	
28	  // MARK: helpers
29	
30	  private func tool(_ name: String) -> Bool {
31	    sh("command -v \(name)", in: NSTemporaryDirectory()).exit == 0
32	  }
33	
34	  private struct MissingTool: Error { let name: String }
35	  private func requireTool(_ name: String) throws {
36	    if !tool(name) {
37	      XCTFail("`\(name)` is required for integration tests; CI installs it (brew install \(name))")
38	      throw MissingTool(name: name)
39	    }
40	  }
41	
42	  private func tempDir() -> String {
43	    let d = NSTemporaryDirectory() + "wr-remote-\(UUID().uuidString)"
44	    try? FileManager.default.createDirectory(atPath: d, withIntermediateDirectories: true)
45	    dirs.append(d)
46	    return d
47	  }
48	
49	  @discardableResult
50	  private func sh(_ cmd: String, in dir: String) -> (out: String, exit: Int32) {
51	    let p = Process()
52	    p.executableURL = URL(fileURLWithPath: "/bin/sh")
53	    p.arguments = ["-c", cmd]
54	    p.currentDirectoryURL = URL(fileURLWithPath: dir)
55	    var env = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment
56	    // Isolate from the developer's own git config — including `push.default`, which is exactly what
57	    // one of these tests is about.
58	    env["GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL"] = "/dev/null"
59	    env["GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM"] = "/dev/null"
60	    env["GIT_AUTHOR_NAME"] = "T"
61	    env["GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL"] = "t@e.com"
62	    env["GIT_COMMITTER_NAME"] = "T"
63	    env["GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL"] = "t@e.com"
64	    env["PATH"] = ShellEnvironment.path()
65	    p.environment = env
66	    let pipe = Pipe()
67	    p.standardOutput = pipe
68	    p.standardError = pipe
69	    try? p.run()
70	    let data = pipe.fileHandleForReading.readDataToEndOfFile()
71	    p.waitUntilExit()
72	    return (String(data: data, encoding: .utf8) ?? "", p.terminationStatus)
73	  }
74	
75	  private func writer(_ vcs: String) -> CLIVCSWriter {
76	    CLIVCSWriter(
77	      vcs: vcs, runner: StatusCommandRunner(), makeProvider: { try VCS.provider(for: $0) },
78	      gate: JJSnapshotGate(maxChainWait: 5))
79	  }

Full suite green: 1628 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed. Lint clean.

**Root cause.** The remotes list was derived from *refs*, not from *config*. `jjRemoteState` built it from `jj bookmark list --all-remotes` — but `jj git remote add` creates no remote bookmarks, so your repo listed only `master` and `@git`, `remotes` came back empty, `primaryRemote` was nil, and the header hit tier [3] "No remote configured". Verified on `workroom-play-jj`: `jj git remote list` shows origin, `jj bookmark list --all-remotes` shows no `@origin` row.

Git had the identical latent bug (`git remote add` writes config, no `refs/remotes/*`), so both paths are fixed.

**Changes** — `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/VCSWriting.swift`:
- `jjRemoteListArgs()` / `gitRemoteListArgs()` — read configured remotes (`jj git remote list`, `git remote`). `--ignore-working-copy` is mandatory on the jj one: without it that command takes the **Git import/export lock**, which no other read here does.
- `parseJJRemoteList` / `parseGitRemoteList` — jj splits on the *last* space (names may contain spaces, URLs don't); drops the `git` pseudo-remote.
- `mergeRemotes(configured:derived:)` — union, config order first, so a failed remote-list call degrades to the old ref-derived answer instead of blanking a working toolbar.

Second defect in the same family, fixed for git parity: a jj bookmark with no `@origin` row left `tracking` nil, which fell through to the fetch tier — the toolbar offered "Never fetched"/Fetch, and fetching can never create the counterpart, so a freshly-remoted repo was permanently stuck. Now reported `gone: true`, so you get **Publish branch** like git.

Tests: 2 integration tests (jj + git, remote added and never fetched), 5 parser/merge unit tests.

Your `workroom-play-jj` should now read "Publish branch — master isn't on origin yet".

without it, it takes the Git import/export lock.

left tracking nil, which fell through to the fetch tier — so a freshly-remoted

1	import SwiftUI
2	
3	/// Every number the VCS toolbar uses, in one place.
4	///
5	/// The horizontal ones are chosen so the toolbar aligns *by construction* with the section header
6	/// beneath it rather than by eye: `outerInset` + `glyphSlot` + `glyphSpacing` puts the branch glyph's
7	/// centre and the branch name's left edge exactly where `SectionHeader`'s chevron centre and title land
8	/// (`InspectorSplitView.headerLabel` uses the same 12 / 12 / 7).
9	enum VCSToolbarMetrics {
10	  /// The tallest thing a text cell stacks: an 11pt semibold title row over a 10pt caption (12pt line),
11	  /// 1pt apart. The title row is 13pt bare but as tall as a `.caption2` capsule — about 15 — whenever a
12	  /// count pill rides it, which is the case this has to budget for.
13	  static let contentHeight: CGFloat = 28
14	  /// Breathing room above and below a cell's content.
15	  ///
16	  /// Expressed as band height rather than as `.padding(.vertical)` on the cells, and that is not a
17	  /// shortcut: `vcsToolbarSegment` fills its cell with `maxHeight: .infinity`, so the content is
18	  /// vertically CENTRED in a fixed-height frame. Padding inside a centred fixed frame is absorbed by the
19	  /// centring and changes nothing on screen — only the band's height actually moves the text off the
20	  /// hairlines. Anyone adding a `.padding(.vertical)` here to "fix the spacing" will see no difference
21	  /// and should change this instead.
22	  static let contentVerticalPadding: CGFloat = 6
23	  /// 40. Two lines genuinely don't fit the section headers' 34pt, so this must exceed them — being
24	  /// taller is also what makes the bar read as its own band rather than a fourth section header.
25	  static let height: CGFloat = contentHeight + contentVerticalPadding * 2
26	  static let outerInset: CGFloat = 12
27	  /// Inner edges of the segments — tighter than `outerInset` so the middle segment isn't starved.
28	  static let innerInset: CGFloat = 8
29	  /// Matches `SectionHeader`'s chevron `.frame(width: 12)`.
30	  static let glyphSlot: CGFloat = 12
31	  /// Matches `SectionHeader`'s `HStack(spacing: 7)`.
32	  static let glyphSpacing: CGFloat = 7
33	  /// Between the inspector's 11pt header glyphs and the pane bar's 13pt action icons: it has to hold
34	  /// against a bold 11pt title without reading as a pane-bar button.
35	  static let glyph: CGFloat = 12
36	  /// 22pt well plus 4pt either side — `ToolbarIconButtonStyle.footprint` rounded to a divider-bounded cell.
37	  static let fetchWidth: CGFloat = 30
38	
39	  static let titleFont = Font.system(size: 11, weight: .semibold)
40	  static let captionFont = Font.system(size: 10)
41	  /// The single-line states. A lone 10pt dim line in the bar reads as a rendering bug, so the solo
42	  /// subtitle is a step up in both size and contrast.
43	  static let soloFont = Font.system(size: 11)
44	
45	  /// ONE floor, shared by the branch and sync segments, because the two are equal width.
46	  ///
47	  /// Equal width is what makes the bar read as two halves plus a button rather than three arbitrary
48	  /// cells, and it's only achievable if both segments have the same floor as well as the same `maxWidth`:
49	  /// an `HStack` divides slack evenly, so unequal minimums stay unequal by their difference at every
50	  /// width. The value is set by the narrowest inspector — `2 × 114 + fetchWidth + 2 dividers = 260`,
51	  /// exactly the 260pt minimum. (It replaces a 100/126 split with a 220 cap on the branch cell; the cap
52	  /// existed to stop a short name hoarding width, which an even division already does.)
53	  static let segmentMinWidth: CGFloat = 114
54	
55	  /// Verbatim from `PRNumberBadge`, so the toolbar's pill matches the ref pill 40pt below it.
56	  static let pillHorizontalPadding: CGFloat = 5
57	  static let pillVerticalPadding: CGFloat = 1
58	  /// The pill's ↑/↓ glyph. Smaller than `glyph` on purpose — it sits inside a `.caption2` capsule and
59	  /// has to read as a direction marker beside the count, not as an icon in its own right.
60	  static let pillArrowGlyph: CGFloat = 7
61	}
62	
63	/// The VCS toolbar: current branch, a sync segment that shows and performs the right remote action, and
64	/// a fetch button — divided into three full-height cells.
65	///
66	/// Lives at the top of `RightInspector`, above the section stack, and only for the Changes activity
67	/// section. Deliberately a plain SwiftUI view inside the inspector's content and **never** a `.toolbar`
68	/// modifier: the window toolbar is kept an empty AppKit `NSToolbar` because a SwiftUI toolbar item's
69	/// overflow `menuFormRepresentation` caused a multi-second app hang.
70	struct VCSToolbar: View {
71	  /// Observed EXPLICITLY, like `HistoryPanel`'s and `FilesPanel`'s models.
72	  ///
73	  /// `RemoteStateModel` is its own `ObservableObject`; `AppStore` merely holds it and does not forward
74	  /// its `objectWillChange`. Reading it through `store.remoteState` alone renders the first state and
75	  /// then never repaints — clicking Push set `inFlight`, ran the push and recorded the result, and the
76	  /// toolbar showed none of it. Caught by `VCSToolbarUITests.testClickingPushRequestsAPush`.
77	  @ObservedObject var model: RemoteStateModel
78	
79	  @EnvironmentObject var store: AppStore
80	  /// `ThemeService.shared` isn't observed by SwiftUI, so a theme switch would otherwise leave the
81	  /// hairlines stale. Same pattern as `ActivityBar`.
82	  @State private var themeTick = 0
83	
84	  private var theme: ThemeTokens { ThemeService.shared.tokens }
85	
86	  /// The toolbar's whole state, resolved in one place so the three segments can't disagree.
87	  private func presentation(now: Date) -> VCSSyncPresentation {
88	    VCSSyncPresenter.make(
89	      state: model.snapshot, hasTarget: model.target != nil,
90	      toolsUsable: store.vcsAllowsRemoteActions(vcs: model.target?.vcs ?? "git"),
91	      // `activeAction`, not `inFlight`: the label must describe THIS workroom. `inFlight` is the
92	      // model-wide lock, so rendering it directly showed "Pushing…" on a workroom that wasn't pushing.
93	      activity: model.activeAction.map { .running($0) } ?? .idle,
94	      failure: model.lastFailure, lastAction: model.lastAction,
95	      pullConflicted: pullConflicted,
96	      // An action is running, but not for THIS workroom. `perform` would drop the click, so the segment
97	      // must not look clickable — see `make`'s `busyElsewhere`.
98	      busyElsewhere: model.inFlight != nil && model.activeAction == nil, now: now)
99	  }
100	
101	  /// Whether our own pull left conflicts that are still unresolved.
102	  ///
103	  /// The live half is read from the store rather than the model because the model has no view of
104	  /// working status — `noteConflictState` is pushed into it once, after the sweep that follows a pull,
105	  /// and is never revised. Reading `workroomStatuses` here means resolving the conflicts in a terminal
106	  /// clears the message on the next sweep, instead of it lingering until the next action.
107	  private var pullConflicted: Bool {
108	    guard let sid = model.target?.sid else { return false }
109	    return VCSSyncPresenter.pullConflicted(
110	      lastPullConflicted: model.lastPullConflicted,
111	      statusConflicted: store.workroomStatuses[sid]?.conflicted == true)
112	  }
113	
114	  var body: some View {
115	    // Only the relative timestamp needs to tick, so `TimelineView` wraps the whole bar but the schedule
116	    // is coarse (30s) and every other value is already `@Published`. Confining it to just the timestamp
117	    // `Text` would need the presentation recomputed per-subview, which is worse.
118	    TimelineView(.periodic(from: .now, by: 30)) { context in
119	      let p = presentation(now: context.date)
120	      HStack(spacing: 0) {
121	        // The branch and sync cells are EQUAL width: same floor, same `maxWidth: .infinity`, and no
122	        // `layoutPriority` on either. All three parts are load-bearing — an `HStack` splits slack evenly
123	        // only between views that are equally flexible, so a priority override or a different floor
124	        // reintroduces the imbalance. (An earlier version gave sync `layoutPriority(1)` AND
125	        // `maxWidth: .infinity`, so it was offered the whole width first and claimed it, pinning the
126	        // branch cell at its floor even in a wide inspector: `feature/login` rendered as `fe…gin`.)
127	        VCSBranchSegment(name: branchName, vcs: model.target?.vcs)
128	          .frame(minWidth: VCSToolbarMetrics.segmentMinWidth, maxWidth: .infinity)
129	        divider
130	        VCSSyncSegment(presentation: p, onAct: { perform(p.action) })
131	          .frame(minWidth: VCSToolbarMetrics.segmentMinWidth, maxWidth: .infinity)
132	        divider
133	        VCSFetchSegment(
134	          isRunning: model.activeAction == .fetch,
135	          isEnabled: model.canFetch
136	            && store.vcsAllowsRemoteActions(vcs: model.target?.vcs ?? "git"),
137	          onFetch: { perform(.fetch) }
138	        )
139	        .frame(width: VCSToolbarMetrics.fetchWidth)
140	      }
141	      .frame(height: VCSToolbarMetrics.height)
142	      .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
143	      .overlay(alignment: .bottom) { theme.border.frame(height: 1) }
144	      .accessibilityElement(children: .contain)
145	      .accessibilityIdentifier("vcs.toolbar")
146	    }
147	    .id(themeTick)
148	    .onReceive(NotificationCenter.default.publisher(for: .themeDidChange)) { _ in themeTick += 1 }
149	  }
150	
151	  /// Full-bleed, unlike `TitlebarDivider` (a 14pt inline group rule) — it's what makes the three cells
152	  /// read as segments rather than as a row of controls.
153	  private var divider: some View {
154	    Rectangle().fill(theme.border).frame(width: 1).frame(maxHeight: .infinity)
155	  }
156	
157	  /// Read through the one accessor every branch-showing surface uses, so this can't disagree with the
158	  /// status bar or the sidebar.
159	  private var branchName: String? {
160	    model.target.flatMap { store.branchName(for: $0.sid) }
161	  }
162	
163	  /// Hands straight to the store, which owns the dirty-tree confirmation gate.
164	  ///
165	  /// The gate used to live here, and that was the bug: the Source Control menu calls
166	  /// `performRemoteAction` directly, so ⌥⇧⌘P autostashed a dirty tree with no warning while this button
167	  /// warned. A gate only one of two entry points honours isn't a gate.
168	  private func perform(_ action: VCSRemoteAction?) {
169	    guard let action else { return }
170	    store.performRemoteAction(action)
171	  }
172	}
173	
174	/// Segment 1: the current branch. **Display only — not a control.**
175	///
176	/// Not a dropdown, and not a button either. Workrooms **are** branches — a workroom's identity is its
177	/// directory name, with no branch field anywhere in the config — so switching a workroom's branch would
178	/// make its name permanently wrong, and the jj equivalent (`jj new <bookmark>`) was reproduced removing
179	/// a file from the working copy and orphaning the workroom's commit. With switching gone there is no
180	/// action left that belongs on the branch name, so this is a label: no `Button`, no hover well, no
181	/// chevron. Each of those would promise something that doesn't happen.
182	///
183	/// It still carries a `.help` — middle truncation hides the middle of a long name, and the tooltip is
184	/// how you read the whole thing — plus a right-click "Copy Branch Name". Neither is a click action.
185	private struct VCSBranchSegment: View {
186	  let name: String?
187	  /// The target's backend (`"git"` / `"jj"`), nil when nothing is selected. Every string in this segment
188	  /// derives from it through `VCSSyncPresenter`, so the caption, the tooltip and the spoken label can't
189	  /// drift out of agreement — and the mapping stays unit-testable rather than inline here.
190	  let vcs: String?
191	
192	  private var noun: String { VCSSyncPresenter.refNoun(vcs: vcs) }
193	  private var caption: String { VCSSyncPresenter.refCaption(vcs: vcs) }
194	  private var theme: ThemeTokens { ThemeService.shared.tokens }
195	
196	  var body: some View {
197	    HStack(spacing: VCSToolbarMetrics.glyphSpacing) {
198	      Image(systemName: "arrow.triangle.branch")
199	        .font(.system(size: VCSToolbarMetrics.glyph))
200	        .foregroundStyle(theme.fgMuted)
201	        .frame(width: VCSToolbarMetrics.glyphSlot)
202	      // The caption is unconditional. It used to sit in a `ViewThatFits` ladder against a name-only
203	      // variant, which dropped it far more often than intended and in the wrong circumstances:
204	      // `ViewThatFits` measures each variant's IDEAL width, and a `.lineLimit(1)` truncating `Text`
205	      // reports its FULL untruncated string as its ideal — so the caption was vetoed by a long *name*,
206	      // never by a narrow cell. jj repos lost it almost always (bookmark names, or the ancestor bookmark
207	      // a workspace's unbookmarked `@` resolves to, run longer than a `feature/login`) while git repos
208	      // kept it, which is exactly the asymmetry that got reported. The name truncates instead; at the
209	      // 114pt floor the caption truncates too, which is honest degradation rather than a silent drop.
210	      VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 1) {
211	        Text(caption)
212	          .font(VCSToolbarMetrics.captionFont)
213	          .foregroundStyle(theme.fgDim)
214	          .lineLimit(1)
215	          .truncationMode(.tail)
216	        nameText
217	      }
218	      Spacer(minLength: 0)
219	    }
220	    .padding(.leading, VCSToolbarMetrics.outerInset)
221	    .padding(.trailing, VCSToolbarMetrics.innerInset)
222	    // The cell's own layout, WITHOUT `vcsToolbarSegment`'s hover fill: that treatment marks a segment as
223	    // clickable, and this one isn't. `contentShape` is still needed so the tooltip and context menu have
224	    // the full cell as their hit region rather than just the glyph and text glyphs.
225	    .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
226	    .contentShape(Rectangle())
227	    .help(name ?? "No \(noun) resolved yet")
228	    // A `Button` was implicitly ONE accessibility element; a plain `HStack` is not, so without this its
229	    // caption and name would be exposed as two unrelated strings.
230	    .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)
231	    // Caption AND name in the LABEL, not split across label + value.
232	    //
233	    // `.accessibilityValue` does not survive on this element: once it stopped being a `Button` and got
234	    // collapsed with `children: .ignore`, AppKit maps it to a static-text element whose value the
235	    // modifier no longer sets — it read back as the empty string, which failed both tests that assert the
236	    // name. (`ChangesPanel`'s combined header shows the mirror-image of the same mapping: there the
237	    // children's text lands in the VALUE and the label comes back empty.) The label is the one field that
238	    // reliably carries what we set, so both parts go in it — and VoiceOver reads it as one phrase, which
239	    // is what a two-line label is anyway.
240	    .accessibilityLabel("\(caption): \(name ?? "unknown")")
241	    .accessibilityIdentifier("vcs.toolbar.branch")
242	    .contextMenu {
243	      // Offered as a menu item rather than making the label selectable: `.textSelection(.enabled)`
244	      // swallows real mouseDown, which would stop this segment being clickable with an actual mouse
245	      // while synthetic test clicks kept passing.
246	      if let name {
247	        Button("Copy \(noun.capitalized) Name") {
248	          NSPasteboard.general.clearContents()
249	          NSPasteboard.general.setString(name, forType: .string)
250	        }
251	      }
252	    }
253	  }
254	
255	  /// `.middle` truncation, because a long branch's distinguishing part is usually its tail
256	  /// (`joel/history-refs-pill`) — the same reasoning the Changes header and status bar already follow.
257	  private var nameText: some View {
258	    Text(name ?? "—")
259	      .font(VCSToolbarMetrics.titleFont)
260	      .lineLimit(1)
261	      .truncationMode(.middle)
262	  }
263	}
264	
265	/// Segment 2: what to do about the remote, and doing it.
266	///
267	/// Line order is inverted relative to segment 1 — bold title over dim subtitle — which is what the
268	/// reference design specifies. The consequence is that the two segments' bold lines do **not** share a
269	/// baseline: both blocks are the same height and vertically centred, so a caption-first block sits low and a
270	/// title-first block sits high. The full-height divider between them is what makes that read as two
271	/// groups rather than a misalignment. Called out because it looks like a bug and isn't.
272	private struct VCSSyncSegment: View {
273	  let presentation: VCSSyncPresentation
274	  let onAct: () -> Void
275	
276	  @State private var hovering = false
277	  @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion
278	  private var theme: ThemeTokens { ThemeService.shared.tokens }
279	
280	  private var toneColor: Color {
281	    switch presentation.tone {
282	    case .normal: return theme.fgDim
283	    case .warning: return theme.warning
284	    case .failure: return theme.failure
285	    }
286	  }
287	
288	  var body: some View {
289	    Button(action: onAct) {
290	      HStack(spacing: VCSToolbarMetrics.glyphSpacing) {
291	        if let symbol = presentation.symbol {
292	          Image(systemName: symbol)
293	            .font(.system(size: VCSToolbarMetrics.glyph))
294	            .foregroundStyle(presentation.tone == .normal ? theme.fgMuted : toneColor)
295	            .frame(width: VCSToolbarMetrics.glyphSlot)
296	        } else if presentation.action != nil, isRunning {
297	          ProgressView().controlSize(.mini).frame(width: VCSToolbarMetrics.glyphSlot)
298	        }
299	        content
300	      }
301	      .padding(.horizontal, VCSToolbarMetrics.innerInset)
302	      .vcsToolbarSegment(hovering: hovering && presentation.isEnabled, reduceMotion: reduceMotion)
303	    }
304	    .buttonStyle(.plain)
305	    .disabled(!presentation.isEnabled)
306	    // Deliberately NO disabled dim, unlike `ToolbarIconButtonStyle`. Every disabled state here is a
307	    // MESSAGE, not a withheld action — "No remote configured", "No repository", "Pushing…", and the
308	    // `.failure`-toned retry line — so all of them have to stay readable; the suppressed hover well is
309	    // what says "not clickable". An `.opacity(0.4)` here also COMPOUNDS: the text is already
310	    // `fgMuted` (fg @ 0.65), so it landed at an effective 0.26, fainter than `fgDim` (0.40) — the
311	    // placeholder tier — and dimmed error copy along with it. That convention's 0.4 is right only
312	    // because it sits on full-strength `fg`.
313	    .onHover { hovering = $0 }
314	    .help(presentation.help)
315	    .accessibilityLabel(presentation.accessibility)
316	    .accessibilityValue(presentation.accessibilityValue)
317	    .accessibilityIdentifier("vcs.toolbar.sync")
318	    // Only when a lock file is blocking the repo. Workroom deliberately doesn't delete it — telling a
319	    // live git's lock from an abandoned one isn't possible from outside the process, and deleting a live
320	    // one corrupts the index — so the fix is the user's to make, and these hand them the file rather
321	    // than making them retype a path out of a tooltip.
322	    .contextMenu {
323	      if let lockPath = presentation.lockPath {
324	        Button("Copy Lock File Path") {
325	          NSPasteboard.general.clearContents()
326	          NSPasteboard.general.setString(lockPath, forType: .string)
327	        }
328	        Button("Reveal Lock File in Finder") {
329	          NSWorkspace.shared.activateFileViewerSelecting([URL(fileURLWithPath: lockPath)])
330	        }
331	      }
332	    }
333	  }
334	
335	  private var isRunning: Bool { presentation.title?.hasSuffix("…") == true }
336	
337	  @ViewBuilder private var content: some View {
338	    if presentation.isSingleLine {
339	      HStack(spacing: VCSToolbarMetrics.glyphSpacing) {
340	        // Centred and a step up in size/contrast: a lone dim 10pt line in the bar reads as broken.
341	        Text(presentation.subtitle)
342	          .font(VCSToolbarMetrics.soloFont)
343	          .foregroundStyle(presentation.tone == .normal ? theme.fgMuted : toneColor)
344	          .lineLimit(1)
345	          .truncationMode(.tail)
346	        Spacer(minLength: 4)
347	        pills
348	      }
349	    } else {
350	      VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 1) {
351	        // The pills ride the TITLE line rather than the whole cell. As siblings of this VStack they
352	        // narrowed BOTH lines, and the line they cost the most was the one that could least afford it:
353	        // the timestamp is the longest string in the bar ("Fetched 22 minutes ago") and the only one
354	        // whose full form is worth reading, while the title above it is short and has an abbreviation
355	        // ladder to fall back on. Now the timestamp gets the segment's whole width and the pills
356	        // compete only with the title, which is what the ladder is for.
357	        HStack(spacing: VCSToolbarMetrics.glyphSpacing) {
358	          // Longest variant first — `ViewThatFits` takes the first that fits, so inverting this order
359	          // silently defeats the whole ladder. `VCSSyncPresentationTests` pins the ordering.
360	          ViewThatFits(in: .horizontal) {
361	            ForEach(presentation.titleVariants, id: \.self) { variant in
362	              Text(variant).font(VCSToolbarMetrics.titleFont).lineLimit(1)
363	            }
364	          }
365	          Spacer(minLength: 4)
366	          pills
367	        }
368	        // The staleness caveat abbreviates but survives. It must NOT be the first thing dropped: the
369	        // count pill it qualifies is pinned, so losing the caveat first would leave an unverified number
370	        // standing alone.
371	        ViewThatFits(in: .horizontal) {
372	          Text(presentation.subtitle)
373	          Text(presentation.subtitleShort)
374	        }
375	        .font(VCSToolbarMetrics.captionFont)
376	        .foregroundStyle(toneColor)
377	        .lineLimit(1)
378	        .truncationMode(.tail)
379	      }
380	      // The cell no longer has a `Spacer` of its own to fill it, so the VStack claims the width — which
381	      // is also what lets the subtitle's ladder measure against the full cell.
382	      .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
383	    }
384	  }
385	
386	  /// Ahead first, then behind — the diverged order the presenter fixes (`↓` before `↑` is decided there,
387	  /// not here; this just renders `badge` then `secondaryBadge`).
388	  @ViewBuilder private var pills: some View {
389	    if let badge = presentation.badge { VCSCountPill(badge: badge) }
390	    if let secondary = presentation.secondaryBadge { VCSCountPill(badge: secondary) }
391	  }
392	}
393	
394	/// Segment 3: fetch.
395	///
396	/// `arrow.down.circle`, not `arrow.clockwise`: the Changes header's Refresh button is already
397	/// `arrow.clockwise` roughly 40pt below and 10pt to the left, and two near-identical circular-arrow
398	/// glyphs meaning different things (re-read local status vs contact the remote) is a real confusion.
399	/// The down-arrow also matches the ↓ direction language of the count pills.
400	private struct VCSFetchSegment: View {
401	  let isRunning: Bool
402	  let isEnabled: Bool
403	  let onFetch: () -> Void
404	
405	  @State private var hovering = false
406	  @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion
407	  private var theme: ThemeTokens { ThemeService.shared.tokens }
408	
409	  var body: some View {
410	    Button(action: onFetch) {
411	      Group {
412	        if isRunning {
413	          // `.mini`, not `.small`: small is ~16pt and would overflow the 12pt glyph slot.
414	          ProgressView().controlSize(.mini)
415	        } else {
416	          Image(systemName: "arrow.down.circle")
417	            .font(.system(size: VCSToolbarMetrics.glyph))
418	            // Unlike segment 2 this IS a bare affordance, so unavailable should read as unavailable —
419	            // but as ONE tier, not a multiply. `fgDim` is fg @ 0.40, the same effective alpha
420	            // `ToolbarIconButtonStyle`'s `.opacity(0.4)` produces on its full-strength glyphs.
421	            .foregroundStyle(isEnabled ? theme.fgMuted : theme.fgDim)
422	        }
423	      }
424	      .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
425	      .vcsToolbarSegment(hovering: hovering && isEnabled, reduceMotion: reduceMotion)
426	    }
427	    .buttonStyle(.plain)
428	    .disabled(!isEnabled || isRunning)
429	    .onHover { hovering = $0 }
430	    .help(isRunning ? "Fetching…" : "Fetch from the remote")
431	    .accessibilityLabel("Fetch")
432	    .accessibilityIdentifier("vcs.toolbar.fetch")
433	  }
434	}
435	
436	/// A count pill: `5 ↑` / `3 ↓`.
437	///
438	/// Geometry and font copied from `PRNumberBadge` so it matches the ref pill in the Changes header just
439	/// below. Both directions use the same `surface` fill rather than hue-coding: the arrow carries the
440	/// direction (shape, not colour) and a count is a quantity, not a severity.
441	private struct VCSCountPill: View {
442	  let badge: VCSSyncPresentation.Badge
443	  private var theme: ThemeTokens { ThemeService.shared.tokens }
444	
445	  var body: some View {
446	    HStack(spacing: 2) {
447	      Text("\(badge.count)").font(.caption2).fontWeight(.semibold).monospacedDigit()
448	      Image(systemName: badge.direction == .ahead ? "arrow.up" : "arrow.down")
449	        .font(.system(size: VCSToolbarMetrics.pillArrowGlyph, weight: .semibold))
450	    }
451	    .foregroundStyle(theme.fgMuted)
452	    .padding(.horizontal, VCSToolbarMetrics.pillHorizontalPadding)
453	    .padding(.vertical, VCSToolbarMetrics.pillVerticalPadding)
454	    .background(Capsule().fill(theme.surface))
455	    // The highest-information 30pt in the bar — it must never yield.
456	    .fixedSize()
457	    // The spoken form comes from the sync button's `accessibilityValue`; a pill read separately would
458	    // just be a bare number with no subject.
459	    .accessibilityHidden(true)
460	  }
461	}
462	
463	extension View {
464	  /// One hover treatment for all three segments: the whole divider-bounded cell fills.
465	  ///
466	  /// Deliberately not the 22pt inset well `InspectorHeaderButton` uses — that's right for a control
467	  /// floating in a header row, but inside a cell whose bounds are drawn by hairlines a small inner well
468	  /// reads as a mistake. Opacity is animated, never the view tree: an implicit tree animation
469	  /// interpolates a glyph's 1pt pixel re-round into a visible slide (see `ToolbarIconButtonStyle`).
470	  fileprivate func vcsToolbarSegment(hovering: Bool, reduceMotion: Bool) -> some View {
471	    self
472	      .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
473	      .background(
474	        ThemeService.shared.tokens.hover
475	          .opacity(hovering ? 1 : 0)
476	          .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .easeOut(duration: 0.12), value: hovering)
477	      )
478	      .contentShape(Rectangle())
479	  }
480	}

1	import Foundation
2	
3	/// What the VCS toolbar's middle segment is currently doing.
4	enum VCSSyncActivity: Equatable, Sendable {
5	  case idle
6	  case running(VCSRemoteAction)
7	}
8	
9	/// Everything the toolbar's sync segment renders, resolved from one state snapshot.
10	///
11	/// A pure mapping, kept out of the view for the same reason as `ChangeBadge`: it's a many-case
12	/// decision that silently drifts. `now` is a parameter rather than a `Date()` read so the whole thing
13	/// is testable at fixed instants.
14	struct VCSSyncPresentation: Equatable, Sendable {
15	  /// Title variants, LONGEST FIRST, for a `ViewThatFits` ladder. Empty ⇒ single-line mode: the segment
16	  /// renders only `subtitle`, vertically centred, at a larger weight.
17	  var titleVariants: [String] = []
18	  var subtitle: String
19	  /// A shorter subtitle for narrow widths. The staleness caveat abbreviates but must never be the
20	  /// first thing dropped — the unverified count it qualifies is the thing that should yield.
21	  var subtitleShort: String
22	  var symbol: String?
23	  var badge: Badge?
24	  var secondaryBadge: Badge?
25	  var action: VCSRemoteAction?
26	  var isEnabled: Bool
27	  var tone: Tone = .normal
28	  var help: String
29	  /// Spoken label. The count pills are `accessibilityHidden`, so their information has to arrive here.
30	  var accessibility: String
31	  var accessibilityValue: String = ""
32	  /// The blocking lock file, when there is one. Carried so the segment can offer to copy or reveal it —
33	  /// the fix is a file operation the user performs, so the least Workroom can do is hand them the path
34	  /// rather than make them transcribe it out of a tooltip.
35	  var lockPath: String?
36	
37	  struct Badge: Equatable, Sendable {
38	    enum Direction: Equatable, Sendable { case ahead, behind }
39	    let count: Int
40	    let direction: Direction
41	  }
42	
43	  enum Tone: Equatable, Sendable { case normal, warning, failure }
44	
45	  var title: String? { titleVariants.first }
46	  var isSingleLine: Bool { titleVariants.isEmpty }
47	}
48	
49	/// Maps a `VCSRemoteState` to what the sync segment shows.
50	///

290	  /// **Exhaustive on purpose — no `default:`.** It used to end `default: return lastAction`, so every
291	  /// failure added later silently inherited "offer a retry", which is the exact defect the `[13]` tier
292	  /// exists to prevent. Two of the failures below were added precisely because they are permanent, and a
293	  /// `default:` would have handed them a doomed button without a compile error.
294	  static func retryAction(for failure: VCSRemoteFailure, lastAction: VCSRemoteAction?)
295	    -> VCSRemoteAction?
296	  {
297	    switch failure {
298	    case .rebaseInProgress: return .abortRebase
299	    case .rejected: return .pull  // the fix for a rejection is to pull, never to force
300	    case .toolMissing, .noRemote: return nil
301	    // Permanent until the user does something outside Workroom: describe the commit, or move off a base
302	    // whose history is protected. Retrying either runs the identical command and fails identically.
303	    case .needsDescription, .immutableHistory: return nil
304	    case .timedOut, .authRequired, .hostKeyUnverified, .dirtyWorkingTree, .other:
305	      return lastAction
306	    // A LOCATED lock file offers nothing, for `rebaseInProgress`'s reason: the file is sitting there, so
307	    // every retry fails identically and the button is a promise that can't be kept. Removing it is the
308	    // only fix and Workroom won't do that for you (see `VCSRemoteFailure.locked`), so the recovery is
309	    // explained rather than offered. An unlocatable lock was transient contention — retry away.
310	    case .locked(let file): return file == nil ? lastAction : nil

314	  /// Whether the pull **we** ran has conflicts still outstanding — the `[14]` tier's condition.
315	  ///

317	  /// pull: a workroom can be conflicted from a merge the user ran in a terminal, and attributing that to
318	  /// the Pull button would be a lie. The live status says they are still there: the flag is cleared only
319	  /// by a new action or a workroom switch, so on its own the message would outlive the conflicts and go
320	  /// on calling a resolved tree broken.
321	  static func pullConflicted(lastPullConflicted: Bool, statusConflicted: Bool) -> Bool {
322	    lastPullConflicted && statusConflicted

325	  /// One-line, actionable copy per failure. The raw stderr is legible for some cases and baffling for
326	  /// others, so the baffling ones get written copy.
327	  static func describe(_ failure: VCSRemoteFailure) -> String {
328	    switch failure {
329	    case .toolMissing(let tool):
330	      return "\(tool) isn’t on Workroom’s PATH."
331	    case .timedOut(let action):
332	      return "\(action.label) timed out."
333	    case .authRequired:

335	      // fails instantly rather than hanging — but the raw stderr is baffling, hence bespoke copy.
336	      return "Couldn’t authenticate. Load your key into ssh-agent, or set a credential helper."
337	    case .hostKeyUnverified:
338	      return "The host’s key isn’t known. Connect once from a terminal to accept it."
339	    case .noRemote:
340	      return "No remote configured."
341	    case .rejected:
342	      return "Rejected — the remote has commits you don’t. Pull first."
343	    case .dirtyWorkingTree:
344	      return "Uncommitted changes are in the way. Commit or stash them first."
345	    case .rebaseInProgress:
346	      return "A rebase is in progress. Abort it to continue."
347	    case .locked(let file):

350	      guard let file else { return "The repository was busy. Try again." }
351	      return "A leftover \(file.filename) is blocking git."
352	    case .needsDescription:
353	      // The most reachable failure on the push path: this is every workroom between the first edit and
354	      // the first commit message. The remedy is one command, so name it.
355	      return "Describe the change before pushing it (jj describe)."
356	    case .immutableHistory:
357	      return "Pull would rewrite shared history here, so it can’t run."
358	    case .other(let message):
359	      return message.split(whereSeparator: \.isNewline).first.map(String.init) ?? "Failed."
360	    }
361	  }

363	  /// The blocking lock file's path, when the failure has one.
364	  static func lockPath(of failure: VCSRemoteFailure) -> String? {
365	    guard case .locked(let file) = failure else { return nil }
366	    return file?.path
367	  }

369	  /// The tooltip form of a failure: `describe`'s one-liner plus, where there is one, the remedy.
370	  ///
371	  /// Only `.locked` currently says more than its subtitle, because it's the only failure whose fix is a
372	  /// thing the user must do OUTSIDE Workroom — and the app deliberately won't do it for them, so the
373	  /// message has to be complete enough to act on: which file, how old, and the caveat that makes the age
374	  /// worth printing. A minutes-old lock with no git running is abandoned; a seconds-old one probably
375	  /// isn't, and that judgement is the user's to make.
376	  static func explain(_ failure: VCSRemoteFailure, now: Date) -> String {
377	    guard case .locked(let file) = failure, let file else { return describe(failure) }
378	    let age = fullFormatter.localizedString(for: file.modifiedAt, relativeTo: now)
379	    return """
380	      A leftover lock file is blocking git.
381	
382	      \(file.path)
383	      Created \(age).
384	
385	      A git command that was force-stopped leaves this behind. If no git command is running for this \
386	      repository, deleting the file is safe:
387	
388	      rm "\(file.path)"
389	      """
390	  }

394	  /// What this backend calls the thing the working copy is on: jj says **bookmark**, git says **branch**.
395	  ///
396	  /// Not cosmetic. A jj bookmark does NOT advance as you commit, which is the defining behaviour of a git
397	  /// branch — so calling it a branch in a jj repo teaches the wrong model of the tool the user is running.
398	  ///
399	  /// A pure function rather than a ternary inside the view because that's the only way it can be tested:
400	  /// the toolbar's caption is not reachable from a unit test, and driving a real jj project through the
401	  /// GUI needs both a selected row and an open terminal.
402	  ///
403	  /// Anything that isn't `"jj"` — including an empty or unrecognised value — reads as "branch". `vcs` comes
404	  /// from the CLI config, so git is the safe default for an unknown, and it matches every non-jj repo the
405	  /// app can currently open.
406	  static func refNoun(vcs: String?) -> String { vcs == "jj" ? "bookmark" : "branch" }
407	
408	  /// The branch segment's caption: "Current Branch" / "Current Bookmark".
409	  static func refCaption(vcs: String?) -> String { "Current \(refNoun(vcs: vcs).capitalized)" }

411	  // MARK: Relative time
412	
413	  private static let fullFormatter: RelativeDateTimeFormatter = {
414	    let f = RelativeDateTimeFormatter()
415	    f.unitsStyle = .full
416	    return f
417	  }()
418	
419	  private static let shortFormatter: RelativeDateTimeFormatter = {
420	    let f = RelativeDateTimeFormatter()
421	    f.unitsStyle = .abbreviated
422	    return f
423	  }()
424	
425	  /// "Fetched 9 minutes ago" / "Fetched 9 min. ago" / "Never fetched" / "".
426	  ///
427	  /// Both forms say "Fetched", never "Last fetched": "ago" already places it in the past, so "Last" only
428	  /// spent width. `short` differs by the formatter's unit style alone.
429	  ///
430	  /// Under a minute reads "just now" rather than "in 0 seconds", which is what
431	  /// `RelativeDateTimeFormatter` produces for a sub-second delta.
432	  ///
433	  /// `.unknown` renders NOTHING — never the word "never". They are different facts: `.never` means we
434	  /// looked and there was no fetch; `.unknown` means we couldn't tell.
435	  static func fetchedAgo(_ lastFetch: VCSLastFetch, now: Date, short: Bool = false) -> String {
436	    switch lastFetch {
437	    case .never: return "Never fetched"
438	    case .unknown: return ""
439	    case .at(let date):
440	      if now.timeIntervalSince(date) < 60 { return "Fetched just now" }
441	      let formatter = short ? shortFormatter : fullFormatter
442	      return "Fetched \(formatter.localizedString(for: date, relativeTo: now))"
443	    }
444	  }

10	@MainActor

14	    case loading
15	    case loaded
16	    case failed(String)

54	  private let ttl: TimeInterval

60	  private var actionTask: Task<Void, Never>?

95	  /// Point the model at a workroom (or clear it with `nil`). No-op if already there.
96	  func focus(_ target: Target?) {

112	  /// just called `focus` eagerly, and retries after a transient failure.

121	  /// Re-read. TTL-gated unless `force` — a watcher can fire several times for one logical change.
122	  func refresh(force: Bool = false) {
123	    guard target != nil else { return }
124	    if !force, let resolvedAt = snapshot?.resolvedAt, now().timeIntervalSince(resolvedAt) < ttl {
125	      return
126	    }

130	  /// Await whatever is in flight.
131	  ///
132	  /// Order matters: an action schedules a refresh when it finishes, so the action must be awaited
133	  /// FIRST and the load task re-read afterwards. Awaiting `task` first captures the pre-action load and
134	  /// returns before the refresh the action queued has even been created.
135	  func awaitCurrentLoad() async {
136	    await actionTask?.value
137	    await task?.value
138	  }

140	  private func load() {
141	    guard let target else { return }
142	    task?.cancel()
143	    state = .loading
144	    let makeWriter = self.makeWriter
145	    let debounce = self.debounce
146	    task = Task { [weak self] in
147	      if debounce > 0 {
148	        try? await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: UInt64(debounce * 1_000_000_000))
149	        if Task.isCancelled { return }
150	      }
151	      let root = URL(fileURLWithPath: target.path, isDirectory: true)
152	      let resolution: VCSRemoteResolution
153	      do {
154	        resolution = await (try makeWriter(root)).remoteState(
155	          path: target.path, projectRoot: target.projectRoot)
156	      } catch {
157	        resolution = .absent
158	      }
159	      if Task.isCancelled { return }

161	    }
162	  }

164	  private func apply(_ resolution: VCSRemoteResolution, for target: Target) {
165	    // A read that finished after the model moved on must not overwrite the new target's state.
166	    guard self.target == target else { return }
167	    switch resolution {
168	    case .state(let state):
169	      // Merge in Workroom's own fetch record. Needed because jj's fetch is invisible: it passes
170	      // `--no-write-fetch-head`, and a fetch that brings nothing records NO operation at all — so the
171	      // op-log scan alone would mean "last fetch that changed something", and clicking Fetch with
172	      // nothing new would leave a stale timestamp on screen. The backend still wins when it is newer,
173	      // which keeps a fetch run in the user's own terminal visible.
174	      snapshot = Self.merging(state, ownFetch: Defaults[.vcsLastFetch][target.projectRoot])
175	      self.state = .loaded
176	      onBranchResolved?(target.sid, state.current.name)
177	    case .absent:
178	      snapshot = nil
179	      self.state = .loaded
180	      onBranchResolved?(target.sid, nil)
181	    case .keepPrior:
182	      // A transient blip — leave the last good snapshot standing rather than blanking the toolbar.
183	      self.state = snapshot == nil ? .idle : .loaded
184	    case .failed(let failure):
185	      snapshot = nil
186	      self.state = .failed(VCSSyncPresenter.describe(failure))
187	      onBranchResolved?(target.sid, nil)
188	    }
189	  }

191	  /// Take the later of the backend's own evidence and Workroom's recorded fetch.
192	  static func merging(_ state: VCSRemoteState, ownFetch: Date?) -> VCSRemoteState {
193	    guard let ownFetch else { return state }
194	    let merged: VCSLastFetch
195	    switch state.lastFetch {
196	    case .at(let backend): merged = .at(max(backend, ownFetch))
197	    case .never, .unknown: merged = .at(ownFetch)

199	    return VCSRemoteState(
200	      current: state.current, tracking: state.tracking, remotes: state.remotes,
201	      primaryRemote: state.primaryRemote, lastFetch: merged, resolvedAt: state.resolvedAt)
202	  }

205

235	  ///
236	  /// `anonymousRevision` matters only for a jj workroom whose `@` carries no bookmark: pushing a bare
237	  /// `@` fails when the working copy is empty and undescribed, which is exactly the state a fresh
238	  /// workroom sits in. Callers pass `CLIVCSWriter.jjPushRevision(hasChanges:hasDescription:)`.
239	  func perform(
240	    _ action: VCSRemoteAction, setUpstream: Bool = false, anonymousRevision: String = "@"
241	  ) {
242	    guard inFlight == nil, let target, let snapshot else { return }
243	    // Aborting a rebase is purely local — requiring a remote would leave a workroom wedged in a rebase
244	    // with no way out from the UI, which is the one state where recovery matters most.
245	    let remote = snapshot.primaryRemote ?? ""
246	    if remote.isEmpty, action != .abortRebase {
247	      lastFailure = .noRemote
248	      lastAction = action
249	      return
250	    }
251	    inFlight = action
252	    inFlightTarget = target
253	    lastAction = action
254	    lastFailure = nil
255	    lastPullConflicted = false
256	    let makeWriter = self.makeWriter
257	    let current = snapshot.current
258	    let tracking = snapshot.tracking
259	    actionTask = Task { [weak self] in
260	      let root = URL(fileURLWithPath: target.path, isDirectory: true)
261	      let result: VCSRemoteActionResult
262	      do {
263	        let writer = try makeWriter(root)
264	        switch action {
265	        case .fetch:
266	          result = await writer.fetch(
267	            path: target.path, projectRoot: target.projectRoot, remote: remote)
268	        case .push:
269	          result = await writer.push(
270	            path: target.path, projectRoot: target.projectRoot, current: current, remote: remote,
271	            setUpstream: setUpstream, anonymousRevision: anonymousRevision)
272	        case .pull:
273	          result = await writer.pullRebase(
274	            path: target.path, projectRoot: target.projectRoot, current: current, remote: remote,
275	            tracking: tracking)
276	        case .abortRebase:
277	          result = await writer.abortRebase(path: target.path, projectRoot: target.projectRoot)
278	        }
279	      } catch {
280	        result = .failed(.other("\(error)"))

282	      self?.finish(action, result: result, for: target)

286	  private func finish(_ action: VCSRemoteAction, result: VCSRemoteActionResult, for target: Target)
287	  {
288	    // Always cleared: the action really is over, and this is the model-wide single-action lock. What is
289	    // NOT unconditional is the RESULT, below.
290	    inFlight = nil
291	    inFlightTarget = nil
292	    // The work happened in `target`'s repo whatever is selected now, so the fetch stamp and the
293	    // downstream refresh belong to it and fire regardless.
294	    if case .ok = result {
295	      if action == .fetch || action == .pull { recordOwnFetch(projectRoot: target.projectRoot) }
296	      onDidMutate?(action, target.sid)
297	    }
298	    // Everything past here writes PUBLISHED state that the toolbar renders for whatever is selected NOW,
299	    // so it needs the same guard `apply` has. Without it, starting a push in one workroom and switching
300	    // to another put the first one's failure — and its action label — on the second one's toolbar,
301	    // reporting a failure for a workroom where nothing was attempted.
302	    guard self.target == target else { return }
303	    switch result {
304	    case .ok:
305	      lastFailure = nil
306	      // Re-read immediately AND let the store refresh everything downstream. The metadata watcher
307	      // would get there on its own, but its coalesce window is ~1s and the toolbar should feel instant.
308	      refresh(force: true)
309	    case .failed(let failure):
310	      // Deliberately leaves `snapshot` intact: a failed action tells you nothing new about the repo.
311	      lastFailure = failure
312	    }
313	  }

315	  /// Stamp Workroom's own fetch time for this project. See `merging` for why this exists.
316	  private func recordOwnFetch(projectRoot: String) {
317	    var stamps = Defaults[.vcsLastFetch]
318	    stamps[projectRoot] = now()
319	    Defaults[.vcsLastFetch] = stamps
320	  }

322	  /// Called by the store after the post-mutation status refresh lands: a pull that reported success may
323	  /// still have produced conflicts (jj writes them into commits and exits 0).
324	  /// `sid` is the workroom the pull ran in — checked, not trusted, for the same reason `finish` checks it:
325	  /// the sweep this waits on is async, so the selection can move before it lands.
326	  func noteConflictState(_ conflicted: Bool, for sid: SidebarID) {
327	    guard target?.sid == sid, lastAction == .pull, lastFailure == nil else { return }
328	    lastPullConflicted = conflicted
329	  }

331	  // MARK: Auto-fetch
332	
333	  /// Fetch when the inspector gains focus, at most once per `autoFetchInterval` per project.
334	  ///
335	  /// Automatic, so it must be quiet: a failure sets `lastFailure` for the tooltip but raises no alert
336	  /// and never blocks the read path. Callers gate on the inspector being visible with the Changes
337	  /// section active, so a hidden toolbar never triggers a network call.
338	  func autoFetchIfDue() {
339	    guard let target, inFlight == nil, let snapshot, snapshot.primaryRemote != nil else { return }
340	    if let last = lastAutoFetch[target.projectRoot],
341	      now().timeIntervalSince(last) < autoFetchInterval
342	    {
343	      return
344	    }
345	    lastAutoFetch[target.projectRoot] = now()
346	    perform(.fetch)
347	  }
