18	/// Why a remote read or action failed.
19	///
20	/// Deliberately NOT folded into `VCSError`: that enum is the backend-*read* taxonomy
21	/// (`lockContention`/`staleSnapshot`/`partialData`/…) and `WorkroomStatusResolver.failure(for:)`
22	/// switches over it exhaustively to choose a sidebar badge. `.authRequired` has no sidebar badge and
23	/// no sensible answer there, so adding it would force a meaningless decision in a function that
24	/// currently has a principled one for every case. Same reasoning that put `CIResolution`/`PRResolution`
25	/// beside their resolver instead of in `VCSModels.swift`.
26	enum VCSRemoteFailure: Equatable, Sendable {
27	  /// `git`/`jj` not on PATH. Distinct from `VCSToolVersions`' floor check, which runs at launch —
28	  /// this is the same condition caught at the point of use.
29	  case toolMissing(String)
30	  case timedOut(VCSRemoteAction)
31	  /// Credentials were needed and none were available.
32	  case authRequired(String)
33	  /// The host's key isn't in `known_hosts`. `BatchMode=yes` turns what would be an interactive
34	  /// confirmation into this, so it needs its own copy — telling the user to configure a credential
35	  /// helper would be wrong advice.
36	  case hostKeyUnverified(String)
37	  case noRemote
38	  /// Push rejected (non-fast-forward). The engine NEVER force-pushes; the UI offers Pull.
39	  case rejected(String)
40	  /// git refused because tracked files would be overwritten.
41	  case dirtyWorkingTree(String)
42	  /// A failed or killed `git pull --rebase` left `rebase-merge`/`rebase-apply` behind. The repo needs
43	  /// `git rebase --abort`, so the UI must offer that instead of a retry that will fail identically.
44	  case rebaseInProgress
45	  /// A repo lock was held — git `index.lock`/`packed-refs.lock`, or jj's `git_import_export.lock`.
46	  ///
47	  /// The payload is the lock file itself when we could find it on disk, and that distinction decides
48	  /// what the UI offers. **`nil` ⇒ transient contention**, so Retry is genuine: another command held the
49	  /// lock briefly and by the next click it is likely gone. **Non-nil ⇒ a lock file is sitting there
50	  /// right now**, and retrying fails identically every time — the same reasoning that makes
51	  /// `rebaseInProgress` offer Abort instead of Retry.
52	  ///
53	  /// A leftover lock is what a SIGKILLed git leaves: the runner escalates to `killTree` two seconds
54	  /// after SIGTERM, and SIGKILL cannot be caught, so git's own cleanup never runs.
55	  ///
56	  /// Workroom does NOT delete it. Whether a lock is truly abandoned or held by a git running right now
57	  /// is not knowable from outside the process — `lsof` can't be trusted for it, and removing a live
58	  /// lock corrupts the index — so this reports and explains, and the removal stays the user's call.
59	  /// That is also what git's own message tells you to do.
60	  case locked(VCSLockFile?)
61	  /// jj refused to rewrite a commit protected by `immutable_heads()` — reached by Pull, whose
62	  /// `jj rebase -b @` moves the whole branch containing `@`, and that branch usually contains a
63	  /// remote-tracked commit. Measured on jj 0.43 for a workroom based off a feature branch while trunk
64	  /// moved on: `Error: Commit 4c8e754829da is immutable`.
65	  ///
66	  /// Offers no retry, for `rebaseInProgress`'s reason: the destination doesn't change between clicks, so
67	  /// every retry fails identically. The real fix is remembering each workroom's own base instead of
68	  /// guessing `trunk()` — filed, not built.
69	  case immutableHistory(String)
70	  /// jj refuses to push a commit with an empty description, changes or not. This is the state a workroom
71	  /// sits in the moment you edit a file and before you write a message, so it is the most reachable
72	  /// failure on the push path, not an edge case. Measured: `Error: Won't push commit 050e657d3c36 since
73	  /// it has no description`.

75	  case other(String)

131	    // A *detail-only* NavigationSplitView: we keep it (vs a plain HStack) only for the window
132	    // toolbar/layering context it sets up — that's what lets the custom title bar, drawn in the
133	    // full-size content under the native title bar, render crisp instead of washed-out by the
134	    // title-bar vibrancy (a plain HStack / NavigationStack doesn't). Its native sidebar column is
135	    // never used (forced `.detailOnly`) — that column is what kept the ~30pt inset-card top gap — so
136	    // the real sidebar is our own `SidebarColumn` in the detail HStack, flush below the bar.

140	    // terminal tab strip's trailing toolbar buttons never lit their hover well — issue #114); the
141	    // title-bar region eats mouse-moved for a raw content view. `NavigationSplitView` hosts the detail
142	    // in an `NSSplitViewController`, which sets up the correct content tracking so `.onHover` fires

3	/// UI tests for the VCS toolbar: its placement above the Changes header, the states its sync segment
4	/// renders, and the button→engine seam.
5	///
6	/// **Every test runs against BOTH backends.** This is an abstract base; `VCSToolbarGitUITests` and
7	/// `VCSToolbarJJUITests` are the two concrete suites, and the only difference between them is the fixture
8	/// project's declared VCS and therefore the vocabulary the branch segment uses. Parity is deliberate — the
9	/// toolbar is one code path with two wordings, and the one defect this structure exists to catch (a jj
10	/// project captioned "Current Branch") was invisible precisely because the suite only ever ran the git
11	/// shape. Where a backend genuinely differs, the expectation comes from `expectedRefNoun` rather than a
12	/// separate test, so neither backend can quietly lose coverage the other has.
13	///
14	/// Remote state is SEEDED via `-WorkroomUITestSyncState` (see `UITestFixture.remoteState`) because the
15	/// fixture's paths aren't real repos — a live read resolves to "No repository", which is a correct but
16	/// uninteresting state. The engine's own correctness against real repos is `VCSRemoteIntegrationTests`;
17	/// what only this tier can see is whether the rendered control does what it says.
18	///
19	/// **The jj suite needs a real `jj` ≥ 0.43 on PATH.** A jj project's remote actions are gated on BOTH tool
20	/// floors (a colocated jj repo drives git underneath — see `VCSToolVersions`), so on a machine with jj
21	/// missing or too old the sync segment correctly disables itself and the state tests fail. That's a true
22	/// dependency of testing a jj project's toolbar, not a flaw in the tests; the git suite has no such
23	/// requirement.
24	///
25	/// **Out of reach here, deliberately:** hover wells and `.help` tooltips (`.onHover` is not driven by
26	/// XCUITest's synthetic hover — see `ChangesPanelUITests`), and the width-degradation ladder (dropped text
27	/// simply isn't in the accessibility tree). Those are covered by `VCSToolbarMetricsTests` (the geometry)
28	/// and `VCSSyncPresentationTests` (the variant ordering and the backend vocabulary).
29	///
30	/// Run with `make app-uitest` on a real GUI login session; excluded from the unit gate.
31	class VCSToolbarUITestsBase: XCTestCase {
32

40

42	  /// that somehow said both.

44	
45	  /// The base contributes no tests of its own — without this, XCTest would run every test three times
46	  /// (once per class) and the base's run would exercise whichever backend the defaults happen to name.
47	  override class var defaultTestSuite: XCTestSuite {
48	    if self == VCSToolbarUITestsBase.self {
49	      return XCTestSuite(name: "VCSToolbarUITestsBase (abstract)")

51	    return super.defaultTestSuite

content.text:
Done. Dialog now carries the failure; bar keeps the one-line notice.

**What happens now.** A user-initiated fetch/push/pull that fails raises a sheet: warning glyph, "Push failed", the full message (never truncated, selectable), a collapsed **Details** disclosure holding the tool's raw stderr in a scrollable monospaced box, and the actions — `Copy`, `Reveal in Finder` (located lock only), `Dismiss` (Esc), and the recovery as the default button (Return). Your case reads:

> Describe the change before pushing it (jj describe).
>
> Give the change a message first, then push again:
>
> jj describe -m "…"

**Design decisions worth knowing:**
- **Auto-fetch stays silent.** It's a network call nobody asked for, so a failure there records `lastFailure` for the toolbar and raises no dialog — `perform(_:userInitiated:)`, `false` only from `autoFetchIfDue`.
- **The bar's behaviour is unchanged.** Same tier, same one-click recovery, same disabled-with-no-recovery rule. Dismissing the dialog doesn't clear `lastFailure` — the failure hasn't stopped being true. Right-click the segment → **Show Error Details…** re-opens it.
- **No doomed default button.** The dialog's primary comes from the same `retryAction` the bar uses, so `needsDescription` / `immutableHistory` / located-lock get no Return-key retry.
- **Hosted on RootView, not the inspector** — ⌥⇧⌘P works with the inspector hidden, and a dialog that only appears when a pane happens to be open is worse than none.
- Recovery routes through `store.performRemoteAction`, so a Pull recovery still meets the dirty-tree autostash confirmation.

Per-failure remedies written for all 11 cases (auth, host key, no remote, rejected, dirty tree, rebase in progress, immutable history, needs description, tool missing, timeout; located lock keeps its existing full explanation).

One gotcha found by the UI test: an `.accessibilityIdentifier` on the sheet's container made SwiftUI absorb every child element — sheet findable, title/message/buttons not. Fixed with `.accessibilityElement(children: .contain)`, and it's commented as such.
